sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section is a placeholder with no text.
The verse about Aaron's staff blossoming almonds is explained in Likkutei Torah, where almonds symbolize speed, alluding to the swiftness of the priesthood's influence.

translations.translation: "And behold, the staff of Aaron had blossomed... and produced almonds."
And it is explained in Likkutei Torah, in the discourse beginning with this verse,
that the reason it specifically produced almonds is that almonds ripen more quickly than any other fruit.
[And Likkutei Torah adds there,
that therefore they are called "shkeidim," from the term "shkidah," meaning haste and speed,
as it is written,
"a rod of an almond tree... for I am hastening (shokeid) My word to perform it."
And it can be said
that the intention of this addition is to hint that the speed inherent in almonds is their essential quality,
and as is known
that the name of a thing indicates its essence],
and therefore they allude to the priesthood,
because the influences drawn down through Aharon the Kohen
[Aharon — the letters spell "ra'ah" (seeing)]
are with speed.
And likewise, this applies to all the Kohanim, the sons of Aharon,
for when the Kohanim bless the people,
influence is drawn down below with great speed, without delays
(as will be explained in section 7).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The root of all influence is from the attribute of Chesed of Atzilus, which descends through the worlds, requiring daily judgment and prayer for it to manifest in physical matters.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
that the root of all influences is from the attribute of His kindness,
the Chesed of Atzilus.
And in order for physical influences—
children, life, and sustenance—
to be drawn from the Chesed of Atzilus, it is through the descent and progression of Chesed through all the levels from Atzilus to Asiyah.
And at every transmission from one level to the next, there is judgment and adjudication
as to whether the influence will be drawn into the lower level or remain in the higher level.
And this is why we pray and ask daily, "Heal us,"
"Bless upon us,"
even though a person's sustenance is fixed for him from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur
(and the intention here in "sustenance" includes all three matters: children, life, and sustenance),
because the writing and sealing for good on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur is the drawing of Chesed into Malchus of Atzilus,
and for the influence of Chesed to be in physical matters, it is through the descent and enclothing of the Chesed of Malchus of Atzilus into the Chesed of Beriah,
and afterward into the Chesed of Yetzirah and Asiyah.
And this is the meaning of "a person is judged every day,"
even though his verdict was already concluded on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur,
because the judgment on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur is that Chesed be drawn to the person in Malchus of Atzilus,
and the judgment in which a person is judged every day is
whether he is worthy that the Chesed already drawn upon his soul above on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur will descend and be drawn
(through Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah until it is drawn)
down into this physical world,
or whether the Chesed will remain above and additional delight will be added for him above.
Therefore we pray every day, "Heal us" and "Bless upon us," etc.,
that the Chesed allotted to him on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur be drawn down into this physical world,
and within this world itself—into physical matters.
And there is another aspect to the daily judgment,
that since the Chesed above is spiritual Chesed,
even after the verdict that it be drawn down into this world,
there is judgment and adjudication regarding which specific matter the Chesed will be drawn into.
Therefore, they instituted praying every day the thirteen middle blessings, which include requests for all the needs of the individual and all the needs of the community.
